bear_case: Counter-argument: Today's equity rally is one leg of a relief trade in a structurally hawkish regime — not a regime change. Two post-close developments underscore the bear case. (1) SPCX $185 stop triggered: SpaceX closed at $174.90 (-8.82%), breaching the $185 daily close stop by $10 — the highest-multiple name in the US market could not hold even with the Iran deal cleared and the entry framework active. If a confirmed geopolitical catalyst can't hold SPCX above its stop, the market's appetite for 84x-revenue growth at a hawkish FOMC is limited. (2) BTC UTC close at $62,952 — Day 1 of the two-day stop clock triggered: Bitcoin diverged from a 1.91% Nasdaq rally, closing well below the $63,500 stop level. Crypto is pricing Fed hawkishness; equities priced Iran relief. These are two different risk frameworks coexisting in the same session. The Fed's dot plot (nine hike projections, 2026 median 3.8%) is unchanged by the Iran deal; DXY held 100.15 despite Brent -5%. The Iran MOU has a 60-day negotiation window with mine-clearance timelines measured in weeks — Iranian domestic opposition is real. A 3-day Juneteenth weekend is the highest-asymmetry hold of 2026. Invalidation: if SPX breaks below 7,460 on Monday's open AND DXY pushes above 101.5, HOLD reverts to STEP_ASIDE. If BTC's Day 2 stop triggers on June 19 UTC midnight, the crypto thesis exits.
